title: When life and practice do not match
issueStatement: What you admire in theory is not yet visible in the habits that keep repeating when no one is watching.
centralInsight: Pure conduct in Gurbani is not moral image. It is what appears when Naam, speech, labor, and hidden motive begin agreeing with each other.
practicalReflection: The fracture hurts because the soul knows the difference between being moved by truth and being reshaped by it.
actionPrompt: Choose one practice today that closes the gap between what you praise and what you permit in your ordinary life.

practice.label: Steady Practice
practice.title: Training conduct until speech and life agree
practice.issueStatement: Integrity weakens when it depends on mood, audience, or bursts of seriousness. The deeper need is a form of conduct that remains true when the feeling is ordinary.
practice.centralInsight: Pure conduct grows by repetition. Honest labor, clean speech, and obedience to the Guru slowly bring the visible life under the same truth the mouth keeps naming.
practice.practicalReflection: Inconsistency is also a practice. If you repeat enough split living, it starts to feel normal; if you repeat enough truthful action, that begins to feel normal instead.
practice.actionPrompt: Keep one repeatable discipline this week that makes your private life more truthful than it was last week.
